summary: Hand-authored subcommands must be attached to their parent through the parent's own variable, before the parent is added to rootCmd. Attaching by searching rootCmd.Commands() for a name at runtime works at execution time but is invisible to any tool that reads the AddCommand graph statically.
reason: `discover patterns` was attached by looping over rootCmd.Commands() and matching on the literal name "discover". The CLI behaved correctly, but verify_skill.py resolves each documented command by walking AddCommand call sites in source, and a loop variable receiver is not resolvable that way. The subcommand never entered the tree, so its own --niche/--sort/--since flags were reported as declared-elsewhere-but-not-on-discover and its name was parsed as a positional argument of `discover`. Binding the parent to a variable first is both simpler and statically analyzable; the failure mode is a docs-vs-source verification error, not a runtime one, so it is only visible when CI runs the verifier against this CLI.
validated_outcome: verify_skill.py went from 6 errors plus 2 likely-false-positive positional-arg reports to 'All checks passed'. `discover --help` still lists the patterns subcommand and `discover patterns --help` still shows --niche/--sort/--since, so the command tree is unchanged.
